title: Can Bangladesh turn US fibre purchases into tariff advantage?
summary:
Bangladesh’s US trade deal set a 19 per cent tariff and tied zero-tariff apparel access to US cotton and man-made-fibre purchases.
A July Section 301 action added a 10 per cent duty and directed three-year textile TRQs for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia.
Quota size, allocation and timing remain pending; gains depend on US fibre costs, legal stability and exporter access.

title: Could US-China compliance escalation raise cotton supply costs?
summary:
China barred parties in China from dealing with six US supply-chain due-diligence organisations, including two cotton-origin testing labs.
The US added 43 China-based firms to the UFLPA Entity List, taking the total to 187, and proposed heightened import disclosures.
Importers using Chinese processing face higher compliance costs, more documentation, working-capital needs and detention risks.

title: South India cotton yarn faces sluggish demand; prices stable
summary:
South India cotton yarn trade remains sluggish as weak fabric lifting keeps buyers cautious; Mumbai and Tiruppur prices stay steady.
Spinning mills seek higher yarn rates to offset rising fibre costs, with Indian cotton yarn becoming more attractive in export markets.
Gujarat cotton is range-bound as buyers await delayed new-crop arrivals, while firmer cottonseed prices support the market.

title: US cotton exports sharply dip but Upland shipments on rise
summary:
US Upland cotton net sales for 2026-27 fell about 71 per cent week on week to 27,500 RB, with India and Vietnam the largest buyers at 10,800 RB each.
Upland shipments rose about 4.7 per cent to 189,500 RB, led by Vietnam, India, Pakistan, Mexico and Indonesia.
Pima sales dropped about 14 per cent to 1,800 RB, while shipments fell about 47 per cent to 4,600 RB.

title: European Commission proposes simpler EU public procurement rules
summary:
European Commission has proposed a regulation to consolidate and simplify EU public procurement rules, moving from five procedures to three.
The market accounts for around 15 per cent of EU GDP and the plan is expected to deliver annual savings of €650 million (~$756 million).
Companies could tender via connected eProcurement platforms under a once-only principle as lawmakers negotiate the text.

title: Textile Exchange unveils first speakers for 2026 conference
summary:
Textile Exchange has announced the first speakers for its 2026 conference, themed ‘The Implementation Era’.
The line-up spans fashion, textiles, apparel, sourcing, sustainability, circularity and forest conservation, with speakers set to explore what a system-wide resilient future could look like, and the actions needed to move the industry towards implementation.

title: Drewry WCI remains stable amid divergent freight movements
summary:
Drewry's WCI stayed stable for a second week, edging up to $4,476 per FEU in the week ending September 10.
Shanghai-Los Angeles rates rose 2 per cent and Shanghai-New York 1 per cent, while Shanghai-Genoa and Rotterdam fell.
Blank sailings, Asian port congestion, Hormuz tensions and Panama Canal transit limits keep early booking important.

title: ICE cotton climbs on stronger crude oil, hopes of Chinese buying
summary:
ICE cotton futures rose for a second day, with December 2026 settling at 88.22 cents as crude oil jumped around 4 per cent.
US heat and adverse weather kept crop-loss concerns alive, while ratings fell to 34 per cent Good/Excellent before Friday’s WASDE report.
Possible Chinese import demand supported sentiment, but a stronger US dollar and weaker ZCE cotton limited confirmation.

title: European Central Bank raises key interest rates by 25 bps
summary:
ECB has raised its three key rates by 25 basis points, with deposit, refinancing and marginal lending rates at 2.50, 2.65 and 2.90 per cent from September 16, 2026.
Middle East-linked inflation pressures reflect the move, adding financing and demand-planning concerns for textile, apparel and retail supply chains, as the ECB projects 2026 growth at 0.9 per cent and inflation at 3.0 per cent.

title: UK sets 40% rail freight growth target by 2040
summary:
UK has targeted at least 40 per cent rail freight growth by 2040, towards a 75 per cent rise by 2050 through Great British Railways.
For apparel importers, manufacturers and retail distribution teams, the aim is clearer capacity planning and stronger domestic supply chains.
The Railways Bill would give Great British Railways powers to support freight growth, network access and investment.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports price to US drops 2.26% YoY in Jan-Jul 2026
summary:
The average price of Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the US fell by 2.26 per cent YoY in the first seven months this year. 
There was also a 6.5-per cent drop in Bangladesh's apparel export value to the US during the period, while shipment volume dropped by 4.34 per cent YoY. 
Not all exporters bore the additional tariff burden equally; in some cases, buyers and exporters shared the cost.

title: Inditex navigates war, tariffs and still delivers
summary:
Middle East disruptions lifted Inditex’s transport and input costs in the first half, affecting gross margin and operating expenditure in the second quarter.
The Zara owner has 480 franchise stores in the Middle East, all open, but geopolitical conditions are impacting regional sales.
First-half gross margin rose 40 basis points to 58.7 per cent, while net income increased 6.8 per cent to €3.

title: India’s US apparel exports fall 26%; Bangladesh overtakes China
summary:
In January–July 2026, US apparel imports from India fell about 26 per cent to $2.45 billion, Office of Textiles and Apparel data show.
Total US apparel imports declined roughly 9 per cent to about $41.8 billion.
Vietnam led at about $9.37 billion, while Bangladesh reached $4.66 billion and moved ahead of China.
Cambodia and Indonesia increased shipments as China fell by about one-third.

title: Argentina apparel imports rise 31.7% in Jan-Jul after liberalisation
summary:
Argentina’s apparel imports reached $468.262 million in January-July 2026, up 31.73 per cent year on year. 
China held a 52.03 per cent share, while Vietnam and Bangladesh grew 50.62 per cent and 54.52 per cent, respectively. 
Imports nearly doubled in 2025 as liberalised trade, easier payment access and price-competitive Asian hubs supported apparel sourcing.

title: US' Caleres lifts FY26 EPS outlook as Q2 sales rise 5.6%
summary:
Caleres expects low-to-mid-single-digit fiscal 2026 sales growth and lifted the lower end of adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50.
Second-quarter net sales rose 5.6 per cent to $695.5 million and GAAP net earnings reached $58.6 million, aided by tariff refunds.
Brand Portfolio sales grew 23.6 per cent, offsetting lower Famous Footwear sales amid a delayed Back-to-School season.

title: Bangladesh, US review trade & investment conditions
summary:
US envoy Brent T Christensen told Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir that US companies are keen to operate in Bangladesh.
The talks covered investment, bilateral trade, energy co-operation, import policy changes and transparency in large infrastructure projects.
For sourcing teams, the discussion points to continued focus on market access, energy supply and business-process reform.

title: US' Lands' End returns to profit as Q2 revenue rises to $302 mn
summary:
Lands' End returned to Q2 FY26 profit, with net income of $3.5 million as revenue rose 2.7 per cent to $302.0 million.
US e-commerce led growth, rising 9.0 per cent to $182.4 million; Outfitters gained, while third-party sales dropped 20.4 per cent.
Lands' End reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with inventory up 13 per cent for seasonal build as operations normalised before the holiday season.

title: US apparel imports are weak; so why did bookings jump 79%?
summary:
US HS61–62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, but the contraction narrowed from 11.82 per cent in Q1 to 3.28 per cent in Q2.
Clothing and accessories-store sales rose 5.9 per cent to $151.09 billion; June's inventory-to-sales ratio fell to 2.14.
US-bound HS61–62 ocean bookings reached 21,434 TEU in June, up 79 per cent, led by Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Australia’s apparel imports dip 7.5% in July 2026
summary:

Fibre imports edged up to Au$12 million, while textile fibre exports declined 9.92 per cent to Au$629 million, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.
Fiscal 2025–26 saw apparel imports down 4.60 per cent and fibre exports up 7.72 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s RMG sector bets on technology for a productivity edge
summary:
Bangladesh apparel exporters are adopting digital monitoring, data-driven production and AI tools to raise productivity, reduce downtime and improve quality.
Some factories report gains of up to 25 per cent versus manual monitoring, though results vary by technology, conditions and measurement.
The shift also raises concerns over worker pressure, privacy and fair sharing of productivity gains.
